original_question: Can one prove the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2), and (3.3) for solutions of the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations without assuming them a priori? Establishing those unconditional regularity estimates would imply global smooth solutions for arbitrary initial data.
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, "Unconditional regularity estimates" (the unnumbered open problem immediately before Conjecture 8.1), read together with Section 3.1, where the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2), (3.3) are defined and used in Theorems 3.1-3.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's main open issue in this part of the survey: whether one can remove the a priori hydrodynamic assumptions (3.1), (3.2), (3.3) from the inhomogeneous Landau/Boltzmann regularity theory. It also correctly captures the consequence emphasized in Section 8.1, namely that proving those bounds would upgrade the conditional regularity theory to global smooth solutions in the inhomogeneous setting.
missing_details: The paper's target is not a numbered conjecture here; it is the unnumbered open problem in Section 8.1, not Conjecture 8.1 or Conjecture 8.2.

The hydrodynamic bounds should be stated explicitly: for all relevant (t,x), 0 < m_0 <= int_{R^d} f(t,x,v) dv <= M_0, int_{R^d} |v|^2 f(t,x,v) dv <= E_0, and int_{R^d} f(t,x,v) log f(t,x,v) dv <= H_0.
These are pointwise-in-(t,x), uniform-on-the-time-interval bounds; your draft names (3.1)-(3.3) but does not say what they are or that the constants are independent of (t,x).

The question concerns the inhomogeneous equations specifically; the paper notes that in the space-homogeneous case the analog of (3.1)-(3.3) is automatic from conservation of mass/energy and entropy monotonicity.

The relevant operators/settings are the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation and the inhomogeneous Landau equation in the boundary-free regimes treated by Theorems 3.1 and 3.2; the draft does not identify the equation form or scope.
The paper's conditional results do not cover the very soft potential regime; that restriction should not be silently dropped when turning the question into a stand-alone one.
For Boltzmann, Theorem 3.1 includes an additional rapid-decay assumption on the initial data in the soft-potential case; your draft omits that nearby technical scope condition.

The paper distinguishes the sharp open problem in Section 8.1 from the weaker global result in Theorem 3.3, where estimates may deteriorate as t -> infinity; your draft does not mention that this weaker unconditional direction is already partially achieved.

The phrase "for arbitrary initial data" needs qualification if the question is to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful: in the paper this implication is understood inside the local-to-global classical-solution framework discussed earlier in Section 3.
The surrounding motivation is the possible formation of implosion singularities, i.e. blowup visible in macroscopic quantities; this is the paper's intended obstruction behind failure of (3.1)-(3.3).
refined_question: In the inhomogeneous, boundary-free Boltzmann/Landau settings considered in Section 3.1 of the paper (namely, the same regimes as Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, so excluding the very soft-potential case), let f(t,x,v) solve partial_t f + v·nabla_x f = Q(f,f) or partial_t f + v·nabla_x f = Q_L(f,f). Can one prove from the equation and admissible smooth initial data alone, rather than assume a priori, uniform hydrodynamic bounds of the form 0 < m_0 <= int_{R^d} f(t,x,v) dv <= M_0, int_{R^d} |v|^2 f(t,x,v) dv <= E_0, and int_{R^d} f(t,x,v) log f(t,x,v) dv <= H_0 for all (t,x) on the interval of existence? Equivalently in the paper's sense, can the hypotheses (3.1), (3.2), and (3.3) in Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 be proved rather than assumed, thereby turning the conditional regularity theory into unconditional global smoothness for the corresponding inhomogeneous Landau and non-cutoff Boltzmann equations?
justification: The draft is aiming at the unnumbered open problem in Section 8.1 because that paragraph literally asks whether the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2), and (3.3) can be proved and immediately states that doing so would yield global smooth solutions for the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations. To make the question stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import from Section 3.1 the exact content of (3.1)-(3.3) and the fact that Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 currently use them as assumptions. One must also keep the paper's scope restriction that these theorems do not include the very soft-potential case, and note the nearby nuance from Theorem 3.3: weaker global smoothness estimates with time-deteriorating constants are already obtained from upper mass/energy bounds plus a propagated lower barrier, so the sharper unresolved issue is the uniform hydrodynamic control itself. Section 7 confirms that this is specifically an inhomogeneous difficulty, since in the homogeneous case the hydrodynamic assumptions are automatic.
